title: Packing Services in Orange County | SOS Moving
metaDescription: Movers and packers in Orange County from SOS Moving: hourly crews pack room by room, boxes billed only when used, free tape and wrap, unpacking on request.
heroSubtitle: Hourly packing crews for Orange County homes: boxes billed only when used, tape and stretch wrap at no charge, unpacking at the new address on request.

faq.question: Is packing in Orange County priced differently from Los Angeles?
faq.answer: The hourly rates are the same, but distance rules change the minimum. For an address 30+ miles out, the minimum becomes 4 hours rather than 3, and time on the road past the 10-mile mark counts twice. Boxes cost from $4 each and only when used; tape and stretch wrap cost nothing.

faq.question: Can you unpack at the new home after an Orange County move?
faq.answer: Yes. Unpacking is part of our packing service, and the crew empties boxes room by room at the new address. Tell us at booking which rooms matter most, usually the kitchen and bedrooms, so the first hours go there.

faq.question: Our Irvine townhome is under a master HOA and a sub-association. What should we send you?
faq.answer: Send the rules from both associations, any certificate of insurance request with its exact wording, and gate or guard instructions. The COI costs $50 and we issue it before packing day. If either association limits work hours, we build the schedule inside them.

faq.question: How do you pack an older house in Old Towne Orange?
faq.answer: We pad door frames and stair rails along the carry path before boxes start moving, and wrap framed and glass items one by one in premium paper or bubble wrap. Let us know which built-ins and fixtures stay with the house so nobody touches them.

faq.question: Can a packing crew come the same day I call?
faq.answer: Often, yes: same-day work is possible when a crew is free. Crews run seven days a week between 8AM and 6PM, so a request that comes too late in the day is booked for the next morning.

faq.question: What will the crew not pack?
faq.answer: Perishables, hazardous materials, firearms and batteries stay out of our boxes. Jewelry, documents and other valuables should travel with you, and so should house plants.
